correctness.rationale: Schur/Jury conditions hold for \(0<\eta,t<1\). Stationary Yule–Walker equations give normalized variance (sigma²/alpha)(A+Bt)/D_eta(t); the mode-wise Gaussian law is unique. The interpolating line through two distinct modes is K+Gt. Real-tap realizability reduces to -1<=G/K<=1+2eta and both inequalities hold strictly by explicit positive factorizations. The difference has exact factor eta(1+2eta)(t-t_-)(t-t_+), proving sign and excluding three distinct zeros. The necessary independent 3x3 Lyapunov solve, interpolation and rational example were reproduced with 1679 exact checks by embedded verify.py. Finite tests supplement, do not prove, the arbitrary-dimensional statement.

value.rationale: Gaussian invariant covariance is a natural accuracy criterion for unadjusted kinetic/momentum samplers; the question is whether one-step-cost temporal correlation can repair spectral bias without full mode-dependent harmonic integration. The result gives the complete two-eigenvalue attainability frontier (both feasible, three impossible), the only feasible noise-power/correlation invariants, and a strict underdispersion/overdispersion map, including a quantified interior deficit. This is a motivated structural design boundary, not a selected small numerical example or table; no general nonlinear sampler guarantee is claimed.
